reason: Behind a reverse proxy that buffers, a browser tab that vanished is noticed only when the proxy closes the connection or when the event stream is rotated at MaxAge (30 minutes by default); until then the ghost holds one goroutine and one stream slot.
justification: Server-sent events are one-way by definition (WHATWG HTML, server-sent events), and a buffering reverse proxy accepts the bytes on the browser's behalf, so a successful write proves only that the proxy took it. The design bounds the cost: MaxAge is configurable and the per-peer cap parks the oldest stream first. Upstream's compression half does not arise.

reason: The order of a job's standard output and standard error relative to each other is approximate: two chunks read in the same round cannot be put back in the order the program wrote them.
justification: Standard output and standard error are two operating-system pipes with no shared clock or sequence number; only the program can merge them by writing both to one pipe. The page labels each chunk with its channel and says that order across channels is approximate, which removes upstream's blind joining of chunks.

reason: A background job and its output buffer end when the host process stops; after a restart the job list starts empty and a request for an old job answers not-found with a plain message.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the records' own words: DH-ADR-JOBS-1 says 'Jobs do not survive the host', and DH-ADR-EXEC-2 says jobs and terminals end with the host because the host holds every process tree it starts; a job that outlived its host would be a process nobody owns. What survives is what the jobs area writes to the session log.

reason: Only the owner can answer an approval or a question; a non-owner who was given access to a session can watch it but cannot answer for it.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the records' own words: DH-ADR-API-5 ships no principal kind other than the owner except the viewer of a live share, 'whose role holds read actions only, because the owner decided that viewers only watch'; owner decision DH-ADR-37 says 'viewers only watch'. DH-ADR-SECURITY-5 allows one answerer per agent. An approval widens what the model may do, so answering stays the owner's.

reason: An attachment upload is one streamed request under the attachment size limit; if it fails part-way the browser sends the whole file again.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-UICORE-8 uploads a file as one streamed request and states 'No resumable' upload in its tradeoff; DH-ADR-API-8 keeps attachment bytes plain, bounded HTTP. A resumable protocol would add partial state on the host that must be cleaned up, to save a retry of a bounded file; the request id still prevents a duplicate attachment.

reason: A terminal survives a page reload but not a host stop or the deletion of its session, and no shell is started again automatically. (Removed: exited terminals no longer count against the terminal limit.)
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-API-7 makes a person's terminal a child process owned by a session, and DH-ADR-EXEC-2 states it in its own words: 'Jobs and terminals still end with the host, because the owners are held by the host process on purpose; a restart keeps jobs story would need a supervisor process and is not designed.' Keeping a shell alive across a host stop would need a separate daemon that owns it, and replaying a shell cannot restore its state. The roster says that the previous host's terminals ended.

reason: Whether a terminal can be opened is known only by opening one: finding the shell program does not prove that the operating system will allocate a pseudo-terminal.
justification: Pseudo-terminal allocation depends on the operating system's state at that moment (the device limit on Unix, the console host on Windows) and neither system offers a probe that reserves one. The design removes the consequence: a terminal is published only after its backend is set up, so a failed creation is a typed error on the form and leaves nothing behind.

reason: An unattended terminal is closed automatically only after it was positively seen idle; a terminal whose activity cannot be observed, or that is busy, is kept until someone closes it, and no maximum run time is imposed.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-API-7 reclaims only on confirmed idleness and states the tradeoff ('a shell whose activity cannot be observed is never reclaimed automatically'), because treating unknown as idle would kill a person's running work. The design narrows upstream's limit: idleness is read from the terminal's foreground process group, not from the shell's prompt.

reason: Only one browser window at a time can type into and resize a terminal, and a window that attaches later gets the current screen and a bounded scrollback, not everything that was ever printed.
justification: A pseudo-terminal has exactly one window size (one TIOCSWINSZ value on Unix, one ConPTY size on Windows), so two windows of different sizes cannot both set it. The scrollback bound is the per-terminal memory limit and is configurable through the execution area's screen settings.

reason: After a reconnect the workspace list is sent whole again; there is no cursor and no replay of the individual changes that were missed.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-WIRE-3 and DH-ADR-API-4 give every small piece of machine state a baseline that is replaced whole, and keep cursors for the session journal only. A value of a few kilobytes cannot be applied out of order and needs no durable change log; the user sees the current list either way.

reason: The file browser lists, searches and watches only inside the session's workspace, while a file named by its path is read wherever the filesystem backend allows.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-API-8 states exactly this split (a listing or a watch explores, a named read does not) so that one read policy, owned by the filesystem seam, decides and the UI layer adds no second, different check.

reason: Register entry U-K2-1, resolved in the convergence round. The filesystem seam's ReadDir now takes a limit and reports truncation (filesystem.md section 6.2): the local provider reads the directory in batches and stops, a remote provider passes the limit to its helper. The files route asks for its entry cap plus one and never more, and draws the sorted partial listing with 'more entries not shown' (DH-D-API-9). Tests DH-T-FS-8 and DH-T-API-24 check with a counting fake provider that no more than the cap plus one entries are requested. The one stat per child was already gone.

An ACP prompt accepts text, resource links and raster images (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF) only, and images only when an attachment store is mounted and the model route accepts them; audio and embedded resources are refused.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words since the final re-check: DH-ADR-SDK-9 has 'Scope boundary of this record (unit acp.acp.2): an ACP prompt carries text, resource links and raster images only, because those are the whole model-input vocabulary of the harness; audio, embedded resources of other types and other content blocks are refused'. Image support is advertised only when the store and the route exist (truthful capabilities).

reason: An MCP server that an ACP client supplies is used for its tools and for reading resources on demand. Its prompt templates cannot be used from an ACP session, and resource subscriptions are not followed.
justification: Register entry U-K2-14, now a recorded boundary. The missing consumer is built in the MCP area (U-K1-7): DH-ADR-CONNECT-4 registers each server prompt as a human command that a person runs and the model can never invoke, and records 'subscriptions are not followed' as scope. Over ACP that command has no way in, because DH-ADR-SDK-9 keeps ACP automation-only and offers no commands. So the ACP carrier's residue is stated by those two records; sdk-acp-typert.md does not say it in its own words, which one sentence in its section on what ACP cannot express would fix.

reason: Through ACP a client cannot replay a transcript (session/load), delete or fork a session, or use modes, commands, plans, terminals, client file operations or elicitation.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-SDK-9 lists these as not offered and DH-ADR-WIRE-7 keeps ACP automation-only, because presentation belongs to the web UI. A program that needs the transcript reads session history on the SDK protocol. Not offering session/load is a recommended default that the owner has not confirmed (sdk-acp-typert.md section 10).

reason: An application's handler in the Go client is told to stop through its context; a handler that ignores the context keeps running in the application's own process after the client has stopped waiting for it.
justification: Go offers no way to stop a goroutine from outside, and the handler is the application's code, not the harness's. DH-ADR-SDK-6 bounds the effect: the late answer is never sent and the host has already settled the request as refused; Close returns after a bounded wait and names the handlers still running.

reason: A pending question or approval lives in one host process: after a restart it cannot be answered, the interrupted turn is closed, and the model may ask again.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-WIRE-4 keeps one in-memory interaction registry that is settled exactly once and says 'Shutdown and transport loss settle pending items as refused', and DH-ADR-SDK-6 settles every doubt, including shutdown, as a refusal. Restoring a pending approval after a restart would let an answer apply to a turn that no longer exists; failing closed costs one more prompt.

reason: Environment files are read once at launch, from the directory the harness was started in and from the harness home; parent directories are not searched and a workspace chosen later contributes nothing.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-BOOT-4 freezes launch facts before the component tree exists, so that a configuration dump shows what actually runs and a directory the model can write cannot change host configuration in the middle of a session. Per-workspace variables for commands belong to the child environment the execution area builds.

reason: A setting changed at run time is written only to the profile layer; the home layer and command-line overlays are read for precedence and never written by the harness.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-LOADER-4 requires exactly one writable layer and DH-ADR-BOOT-2 says which. The cost is bounded: an edit that a higher layer shadows is refused with that layer's name and file, and the other layers are plain files whose hand edits the same reload picks up.

reason: The running plugin manager refuses to disable or remove protected entries (required entries and its own components), manages only the profile it runs in, and does not edit an agent preset's composition. The model's own tool changes nothing in a profile at all: it can only attach a plugin to its session.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-BOOT-10 says 'Protected entries are refused', so the management surface cannot remove itself, and that the model-facing tool 'changes nothing in the profile'; owner decision DH-ADR-30 limits that tool to list, inspect, attach and detach. The clause 'manages only the profile it runs in' is not in a record's own words: boot.md section 6 says another profile is managed from the command line, which composes it without a running host. A sentence in DH-ADR-BOOT-10 would close that.

reason: The inspection tool (harness_inspect) only reads: it cannot call a service, change configuration or run code. Upstream's other half, a query that needed a responding browser page, is gone because every provider lives in the host.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-EXT-9 makes inspection host-only, read-only and generated ('no provider method changes anything'), so that a tool which shows the composition is not a second way to change it. Changes go through settings and plugin management, each with its own approval and audit.

reason: A macOS Developer ID signature with notarization and a Windows code signature can be produced only with the real certificates inside the protected release environment, so that part of a release cannot be rehearsed elsewhere.
justification: Apple's notarization service and Windows Authenticode vouch for a publisher through certificates the publisher must hold; no design of the harness changes that. DH-ADR-ELECTRONBUILDER-2 keeps signing in the tag-triggered release workflow. The other half of upstream's limit is removed: the update path is qualified against a private feed with a test key (DH-ADR-ELECTRONUPDATER-1). Which certificates and where the keys are kept is still open with the owner.

reason: The fault-injecting model server's random mix of failures is test pressure chosen by the test author, not an estimate of how often a real provider fails.
justification: How often a model provider fails is a property of that third-party service, which publishes no distribution; a fixture cannot know it. DH-D-UTIL-6 keeps the seeded mix and prints the seed so that a run can be repeated, and a caller with measured weights can supply them.

reason: A replay can derive everything the session log recorded, now including a failure before the first chunk and summariser calls, but a model call that never returns is not in the log and must be written by hand in an override file.
justification: A session export is a finite list of events, and a wait that never ended has no event to record. The Go design narrows upstream's limit to exactly that case: every attempt, failed ones included, is one logged event (DH-ADR-UTIL-7, DH-D-UTIL-7).

reason: Upstream's limit was a leftover of a migration: some snapshot behaviours could not move off the ACP adapter. The Go replay runner has one driver per surface behind one interface and every scenario names the driver it needs, so a behaviour whose stimulus is an ACP client is driven through ACP by design and no adapter is a remainder.
A file whose name and extension are not in the language table is shown as plain text with no highlighting, even when its content is unambiguous; the table never reads content.
justification: Deliberate, so that the same file renders the same way everywhere and bytes written by the model cannot change rendering; the only content verdict is text or binary, in the filesystem area. DH-ADR-UTIL-9, added in the convergence round as a recommended default, states the rule (item a) and DH-D-UTIL-5 builds it.

reason: Identifiers are random and unique only with overwhelming probability; the identifier helper itself detects no collision.
justification: This is the mathematics of random identifiers with 122 random bits (RFC 9562 version 4), not something a design removes. Where uniqueness matters the store enforces it with a key constraint, so a collision would be a refused insert and never silent sharing (DH-ADR-NODECRYPTO-2).

reason: The file name offered for an exported item is derived from its declared media type, and an explicit suffix wins; the content is not inspected to guess a format.
justification: Deliberate: media types are answered from the name by one compiled-in table so that the answer is the same on every machine. DH-ADR-UTIL-9, added in the convergence round as a recommended default, states the rule (item a) and DH-D-UTIL-5 builds it.

reason: In a configured path only a bare ~ and ~/ expand to the home directory; named-user forms such as ~alice, environment variables and shell expressions are left as written.
justification: Deliberate: expanding variables or shell syntax in a path would evaluate a configuration value against the environment outside the one explicit mechanism for that, the restricted expression language of DH-ADR-LOADER-3. DH-ADR-UTIL-9, added in the convergence round as a recommended default, states the rule (item b) and DH-D-UTIL-5 builds it.

reason: A network whose proxy is given only by a proxy auto-configuration (PAC) file still needs the user to export the proxy variables; the launch now names the PAC address and says so. Removed in the convergence round (register entry U-K2-2): the static proxy set in the Windows or macOS system settings is read once at launch, below every environment variable. SOCKS5 proxy URLs already worked.
justification: Deliberate for the part that remains: DH-ADR-UTIL-10 states that a PAC address is reported and never fetched or evaluated, because evaluating one needs a script engine the design does not have (DH-ADR-8). The same record designs the static reader (tests DH-T-UTIL-21, scenario DH-E-UTIL-4). One fact behind it is still unverified and recorded as open in util-test-support.md section 10: that the Windows registry values can be read in a build without cgo. If they cannot, Windows has no reader and keeps the old limit; the design says so. The static reader is deliverable DH-D-UTIL-9 since the split of the fix pass.

reason: A third-party program the host starts (a Node-based MCP server, for example) goes through the proxy only if that program's own runtime reads the proxy variables it is given.
justification: How a third-party program opens its connections is that program's behaviour; a parent process can only hand over the environment. DH-D-UTIL-2 gives a trusted child the user's own values and the resolved ones for names the user left unset (DH-ADR-UTIL-5). The host itself no longer depends on any Node version.

reason: Register entry U-K2-3, resolved in the convergence round. util-test-support.md section 6.2 adds an import-graph gate: test DH-T-UTIL-22 lists every package in the dsh binary's import graph, dependencies included, that imports a package able to open a connection, and compares the list with a reviewed table in which each entry says how its client is supplied by egress or why it never dials. A dependency that adds such a package fails the gate until reviewed. The gate shows which packages can dial, not that they do, so the recording transport of the egress tests stays (DH-D-UTIL-2). The gate is deliverable DH-D-UTIL-10 since the split of the fix pass.
The launch environment is read once from the directory the harness was started in; a workspace chosen later in the web UI contributes no environment values.
justification: Deliberate, and the same boundary as unit boot.app-boot.6: DH-ADR-BOOT-4 freezes launch facts before the tree exists, because following a workspace would let a directory the model can write change the harness environment in the middle of a session.

reason: On Windows, opening the web UI in the default browser needs an interactive desktop session; started from a service, a scheduled task or an SSH session the hand-off can report success having opened nothing.
justification: Windows runs services and SSH sessions in a non-interactive session where the shell launches no file association; the harness cannot change that. The launch always prints the URL as well and the hand-off has a deadline, so a failed open costs only the convenience (DH-LIB-OPEN).

reason: The filter of a pick-list matches substrings and letters in order from a word start; a transposed or wrong letter (pluign for plugin) finds nothing.
justification: Deliberate: a filter that also guesses at typing errors returns matches the user cannot explain, and the match tiers are fixed by golden tests so that order is predictable. DH-ADR-UTIL-9, added in the convergence round as a recommended default, states the rule (item c: the filter 'tolerates no typing error'); DH-D-UTIL-12 builds it.

reason: The pick-list filter is not the ranker used for file references in the composer; that one is a separate ranker in the filesystem area's search package. Upstream's second separate index, the plugin market, is not built at all.
justification: Deliberate: ranking paths in a large tree is a different problem from filtering a short list. DH-ADR-UTIL-9, added in the convergence round as a recommended default, states the two-ranker split (item d); the market half is DH-ADR-13 (no plugin discovery).

reason: A schedule accepts a bounded subset of recurrence rules: five-field cron and the RRULE subset upstream accepts, with limits on density and range; anything else is refused with the cause (syntax, zone, density or range).
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-RRULE-1 says 'The accepted subset and limits of R1 to R3 are kept from upstream unchanged', because the subset is what the model was taught and the limits guarantee bounded work when occurrences are resolved after a long downtime. Built by DH-D-UTIL-11 since the split of the fix pass.

reason: A deadline is a notification: cancelling a context cannot stop work that ignores it, so every capability keeps its own way to end a process, a socket or a task.
justification: The Go runtime has no operation that stops a goroutine from outside. The design bounds the effect: process-owning code ends the process tree, and a conformance helper in DH-D-UTIL-6 fails any tool body that does not return when its context ends (DH-ADR-UTIL-4).

reason: When a cancellation from above arrives before a local timer fires, the record says cancelled and cannot also say that the timeout would have fired.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-ARCH-3 records one typed cause per cancellation on turn/end and says '"First cause wins" is the standard library's behaviour', which is what makes the record unambiguous; DH-ADR-UTIL-4 makes every deadline a context.WithTimeoutCause.

reason: The idle timer on a response body measures silence on the wire only; it is not a limit on total time and does not count the consumer's own pauses.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words since the final re-check: DH-ADR-UTIL-4 has 'Scope boundary of this record (unit util.timeout.4): egress.IdleBody bounds silence on a response body, not its total length, because a model's streamed answer may legitimately run for many minutes while bytes keep arriving; a caller that needs a total limit sets its own context deadline'.

reason: The acp profile reads its configuration once: an edit to a configuration layer takes effect at the next start, not while a client is connected.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-BUNDLE-1 says in its title that only web follows configuration edits and in its tradeoff that 'Stdio and one-shot profiles need a restart to see a configuration change'. A reload that restarts a spine entry would unload the ACP server and its agents, and the restarted server would have to claim standard input and output a second time. The acp profile is deliverable DH-D-BUNDLE-8 since the split of the fix pass.

reason: Upstream's bullet described a Windows-only difference: other platforms granted the real temporary areas, Windows granted a private per-session directory, and read-only granted nothing. DH-ADR-SANDBOX-4 gives every confined start on every platform the session's own scratch directory as a write root and as TMPDIR, TMP and TEMP, also under read-only, and lists the actual paths to the model. The private directory is now the stated contract on all platforms and not a Windows exception.
A headless run answers one task and exits; there is no interactive follow-up in the same process. A later run continues the conversation with the session option.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words since the final re-check: DH-ADR-BUNDLE-9 has 'Scope boundary of this record (units bundle.headless.1, bundle.headless.9): dsh headless runs one task, or resumes one session for one more task, and exits; it is not a daemon or a queue, because unattended long-lived work is the web host's job and a one-shot run must end so that its exit status means something'.

reason: Register entry U-K2-4, resolved in the convergence round. app-cli.md (the dsh headless row of the command table and the output rules of section 6.2, under DH-ADR-CLI-3) has a headless run write one progress line to the diagnostic stream when the run starts and one at each step start, before any token, naming the step and the model route and holding no model output. Test DH-T-CLI-12 checks that the line precedes the first token of every step. A recommended default the owner has not confirmed.

Register entry U-K2-4, resolved in the convergence round. dsh headless gains the option --reasoning auto|show|hide (app-cli.md, under DH-ADR-CLI-3). The default, auto, writes reasoning to the diagnostic stream only when that stream is a terminal, so a log collector that keeps standard error no longer keeps model output unless the operator asks with show. Test DH-T-CLI-12 checks all three values against a buffer and a pseudo-terminal. A recommended default the owner has not confirmed.
Standard output of a headless run carries only the final answer; intermediate tool output appears only with the JSON option, which prints the complete event log.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words since the fix pass: DH-ADR-CLI-3 has 'Scope boundary of this record (unit bundle.headless.8): the result stream carries only the result, so dsh headless without --json prints the final answer and nothing else there'.

reason: A headless run refuses to continue a session that was recorded in another working directory, a subagent's session, or a session another process currently holds. (Removed: a session recorded under a preset is no longer refused.)
justification: Deliberate, and all three clauses are now stated in the records' own words: DH-ADR-BUNDLE-9 says 'A resume is refused for a session created in another working directory (its file tools would act on a different tree than the operator named) and for a subagent's session (it belongs to its root); a session held by another process is refused by DH-ADR-12'. DH-ADR-BUNDLE-3 removes the preset clause by composing every agent through a preset.

reason: The sdk profile starts no web server, so file cards and opening a file are the embedding program's job. Narrowed: a web host on the same home lists and shows the sessions an SDK host wrote.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words since the final re-check: DH-ADR-BUNDLE-1 has 'Scope boundary of this record (unit bundle.sdk-app.1): the stdio profiles (sdk, sdk-minimal, acp) mount no web listener, because the program that started the process owns it and talks over its pipes; a person who wants to watch the same sessions in a browser runs dsh web on the same home' (DH-ADR-12).

reason: Register entry U-K2-5, resolved in the convergence round. The SDK protocol carries an optional timeZone (an IANA zone name) on initialize, with an override on session/create (sdk-acp-typert.md section 6.2). The host validates the name and refuses an unknown one; the clock context uses it as the user's zone, says 'unavailable' only when none was given, and never presents the host process's zone as the user's. The Go and Python clients expose it as an option. Test DH-T-SDK-25. A session driven over ACP keeps the limit, because that protocol has no such field; the specification says so.
A question from the model needs someone to answer it: when the SDK client registered no answerer, the question tool call is settled as unavailable with the reason.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-SECURITY-5 fails closed when nobody answers, and DH-ADR-HUMAN-2 has answerers register per channel with nothing transferring automatically. Whether the question tool should be hidden from the model when no answerer is bound is an open request to the human-interaction area (section 10 of bundle-preset.md).

reason: A schedule fires only while some host process is running on the harness home; occurrences missed while none ran are reported, not replayed.
justification: Deliberate: the product has no background service. DH-ADR-JOBS-7 has a due occurrence claimed in the database and delivered by a process that can write the target, and DH-ADR-JOBS-6 fixes latest-only catch-up. A schedule made in an SDK session is stored in the shared home, so any later host on that home delivers the next occurrence.

reason: Saved plugin and configuration changes belong to one profile of one harness home, so two embedding programs that use the same home and profile share them. (Upstream's other half, a Python launcher needing Node and pnpm, cannot arise.)
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-BOOT-2 makes the profile layer the one writable layer, which is shared state by definition. An embedding that wants its own composition names its own profile (one small file that extends sdk) or its own home, and per-launch overlays change nothing on disk (DH-ADR-BUNDLE-1).

reason: The sdk profile reads its configuration once: an edit to a configuration layer takes effect at the next start.
justification: Deliberate, and the same boundary as unit bundle.acp-app.3: DH-ADR-BUNDLE-1 says only web follows configuration edits and 'Stdio and one-shot profiles need a restart to see a configuration change', because a reload would unload the SDK server and its agents and the restarted server could not claim standard input and output a second time.

reason: The minimal profile leaves out the product services (settings, managed credentials, policy presets, telemetry, web tools, the full tool roster) on purpose.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-BUNDLE-2 makes the minimal profile a subset of the full one, so that an embedding or evaluation run gets an explicit kernel and the profile proves the spine runs without product services. Because it is a subset and not a copy, adding one service is one insert in the profile layer. The sdk-minimal profile is deliverable DH-D-BUNDLE-8 since the split of the fix pass.

reason: Reading an image needs a model that accepts image input; with a text-only model the image tool returns an error.
justification: Whether a model accepts images is a property of the third-party model the operator selected, not of the harness. Upstream's fixed storage directory is gone (images go through the attachment store). Whether the tool is hidden when the route takes no images belongs to the filesystem and model areas.

reason: TLS is something the operator turns on by naming a certificate and key; the harness obtains and renews no certificate. (Removed: a renewed certificate file is picked up without a restart.)
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-HOST-2 requires TLS or an explicit flag for a network listener and now states in its tradeoff that the harness obtains and renews no certificate and that the operator supplies the pair, because issuing one needs a name, a challenge path and a trust decision that belong to whoever runs the machine. Obtaining one would also add outbound requests and a renewal duty to a local tool (DH-ADR-9).

reason: The host knows only that it asked the operating system to open a browser, not that a browser window appeared or that it was later closed; the printed URL is the manual fallback.
justification: The operating systems' launchers (xdg-open, open, the Windows shell) return before the browser shows anything and report nothing afterwards; no portable call gives the outcome. The Go host does see a launch token being exchanged, which shows that some browser signed in.

reason: When the harness is started in an SSH session it prints the URL and opens no browser; the user's SSH client or editor must forward and open the address.
justification: A browser started on the remote machine cannot appear on the user's screen; only the forwarding client on the user's machine can open the local address. This is a fact of remote sessions, not a missing feature.

reason: The BROWSER override that chooses the program for the automatic hand-off is taken only from the inherited process environment, never from an environment file found in a directory.
justification: Deliberate security rule: DH-ADR-BOOT-4 forbids a discovered file from setting a launch-only name, among them the names of programs the host starts, so that a file in a project directory cannot choose a program for the host to run.

reason: The web listener cannot be bound to all network interfaces: a wildcard address is refused at start-up and the operator must name one concrete address.
justification: Deliberate security rule: DH-ADR-API-6 lists a wildcard bind among the refused start-ups, because whoever reaches the listener with a launch URL is the owner and can run commands, so binding every interface must never happen by default or by accident.

reason: A preset is not a security boundary, and an old revision of a preset is not kept across a restart: a resumed session binds the definition that is current. (Removed: configuration can no longer execute host code, and a user override no longer replaces the whole child list.)
justification: Deliberate: a running revision is live component state and cannot be stored. DH-ADR-BUNDLE-6 says 'Resume binds the current definition of the recorded id' and that a resumed session can still get a different composition, which the log now records with a digest. DH-ADR-BUNDLE-4 makes children a keyed map that layers merge into. The clause 'a preset is not a security boundary' is stated in the limitations of bundle-preset.md section 10, not in a record; it is a description of what a preset is rather than a limit a person meets.

reason: The persona component can be mounted only inside a preset. Mounted at the top level it fails to load with a message that names the prompt component's persona field, which is where a deployment-wide persona is set.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words since the final re-check: DH-ADR-BUNDLE-4 has 'Scope boundary of this record (unit preset.persona.1): the persona component mounts only as a child of an agent preset and refuses to load at the top level, because who the agent is belongs to one composition; a global persona would silently apply to every preset and undo their differences'. Test DH-T-BUNDLE-16 checks the refusal.

reason: An upload is one streamed request per file; a failed or cancelled transfer starts again from the first byte. Narrowed: files are sent one at a time, so only the failed file is repeated, and files already stored stay staged across a reload and a host restart.
justification: Deliberate, and the same boundary as unit api.session-controller.4: DH-ADR-UICORE-8 uploads a file when it is picked as one streamed request, and DH-ADR-API-8 keeps attachment bytes plain, bounded HTTP. Resumable offsets would need partial objects in a store that verifies a digest over the whole object.

reason: Usage events wait in memory only and no warehouse acknowledges them, so events are lost on overflow, on a failed send and when the host exits; the loss is counted and shown. (Removed: there is no browser-side sender whose failures are discarded.)
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-HOST-7 keeps every reporting channel memory-only and has it report each batch's outcome, because a durable outbox would keep usage data on disk and would have to be purged whenever consent is withdrawn. DH-ADR-UICORE-9 records usage on the host from a closed catalogue and sends nothing until the user opts in.

reason: Some key combinations cannot be used as shortcuts because the browser keeps them for itself, so web defaults use longer chords and a few commands have no default key; every command still has a visible control.
justification: A web page never receives a chord the browser reserves (new tab, close tab, settings and others, different per browser and operating system). Upstream's desktop application intercepted keys natively; DH-ADR-18 removed it. DH-ADR-UICORE-6 states that the browser's own keys stay with the browser.

reason: An open context menu belongs to one browser tab and is gone when the tab closes; it is not written to the session log.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words since the final re-check: DH-ADR-UIKIT-5 has 'Scope boundary of this record: an open menu is view state of one browser tab, gone when the tab closes, and is never written to the session log or any store, because a menu changes nothing by being open and what an item does is recorded by the route it calls'.

reason: When a side pane opens or is resized the transcript reflows, and in a browser without scroll anchoring the line the reader was on can move out of view.
justification: Reclassed from platform limit in the re-sweep: a script could keep the reading position, so the limit follows from a design choice, not from the browser alone. DH-ADR-UICHAT-8 makes the choice in its own words: 'this area adds no reading script', and its tradeoff says 'Where a browser lacks scroll anchoring an inserted page may shift the view'. The server-rendered transcript leaves CSS scroll anchoring enabled, so engines that have it keep the line.

reason: The status mark has five states (done, warning, ongoing, error, idle) and no 'active' state.
justification: Reclassed from not applicable in the re-sweep (the Go design builds the same five-state mark), and stated in the record's own words since the final re-check: DH-ADR-UIKIT-1 has 'Scope boundary of this record: the status mark has exactly five states (done, warning, ongoing, error, idle) and no active state, and a sixth state is added only when a consumer needs one, because each variant is a typed constant that every view, its stylesheet and its accessible name must handle'.

reason: The frame that shows a command's output replays only line-level control (colours, carriage return, backspace, erase in line, tabs); output from a program that addresses the cursor or switches screens is shown with those sequences stripped.
justification: Deliberate: command output is an unbounded stream of lines, while cursor addressing needs a fixed grid with bounded history; an interactive program belongs in the terminal island, which is a real emulator. DH-ADR-UIKIT-3 states it since the convergence round ('the frame that shows a command's output is not a terminal emulator'), and requirement R2 of DH-LIB-ANSER carries the detail.

reason: A comparison of two texts is bounded: beyond the bound the view shows a coarse whole replacement, flagged as such, instead of a line-by-line alignment.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-DIFF-1 keeps one diff package on the host, bounded by input size, because an unbounded diff of model-controlled text is a denial of service. The bound is now a rule of the two texts alone, computed once on the host, so the same edit always renders the same way and the browser allocates nothing.

reason: Only a fixed list of well-known sites gets its own icon next to a link; every other link keeps the generic globe.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the records' own words since the fix pass: DH-ADR-UIKIT-6 has 'Scope boundary of this record: site marks are a fixed list of known sites shipped in a sprite; a site not on the list gets a generic mark, because fetching a site's own icon would tell that site what the reader is looking at', and DH-ADR-9 has the same sentence. The list is data in the binary and grows by one symbol and one table row.

reason: While a reply is still streaming, a reference-style link or a footnote whose definition arrives later is shown as literal text; it is drawn correctly once the reply is complete.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-REACT-2 sends streaming text as block-level deltas and freezes finished blocks, and says in its tradeoff 'A reference-style link whose definition arrives after its block froze stays literal until the message settles'. Resolving a late definition would mean re-rendering frozen blocks on every chunk.

reason: A very long source line is shown without syntax colours, and a comment or string that opens on it can mis-colour the lines after it. (Removed: highlighting runs on the host and cannot freeze the page.)
justification: Reclassed from platform limit in the re-sweep (audit Q3-3), and stated as a choice in the record's own words since the final re-check: DH-ADR-UICONV-4 has 'Scope boundary of this record, code highlighting: a source line longer than the cut-off of DH-LIB-SHIKI-R3, and a block above its size limit, is shown as one plain run ... This is kept on purpose, not forced by a platform: highlighting runs on the host for every viewer, so its cost must be bounded per render, and the chosen tokeniser (chroma) backtracks and needs its per-rule time limit', with DH-ADR-15 ruling out a native engine. The loss is cosmetic.

reason: A shortcut is bound to a physical key position and shown with its US-layout key name, browser-reserved combinations cannot be bound, and only components that are loaded contribute rows to the shortcut table.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-UICORE-6 registers shortcuts as host commands, declares defaults 'with physical key codes', and says in its title that 'the browser's own keys stay with the browser'; with no desktop application (DH-ADR-18) there is no other window. Rows from loaded components only is how owned lifetimes are meant to work.

reason: The UI offers Download but not Save as, and copying an image needs the browser's clipboard permission. (Removed: the copy no longer depends on the browser decoding the image, because the host serves a PNG.)
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-UICHAT-9 drops save-as with the desktop application that offered it (DH-ADR-18). A web page cannot choose where a download is saved or grant itself clipboard access; the browser's own setting can ask for a location.

reason: After a download the page cannot offer to show the saved file in its folder, because it is never told where the file went.
justification: No browser reports a download's destination to the page that started it; the browser's own downloads list has the reveal action. For a file that already exists in the workspace the host path is known and its open-in-folder action belongs to the area that opens host files.

reason: Dragging a file out of the page into another application works only in Chromium-family browsers; elsewhere the user downloads the file. (Removed: application-local tokens and the unreadable cross-origin image case.)
justification: The web platform has no cross-browser way to hand an original file to another application during a drag; only Chromium implements the DownloadURL drag type. The native path existed only in the desktop application removed by DH-ADR-18 (DH-ADR-UICHAT-9). The scenario records the browsers where drag-out is unsupported.

reason: A file mention in a sent message does not follow a later rename or deletion of the file: it shows what was true when the message was accepted. (Removed: the answer no longer depends on the page load; every tab and every reload draws the same thing.)
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-UICHAT-2 fixes what a sent mention shows at admission and says 'A sent mention does not follow a later rename', so that a rendered fragment is a function of the session log alone and a replay draws what the live stream drew. The chip opens the file preview, which shows a missing file as missing.

reason: A credential that follows no published format is shown as written, and values after names such as password= are not masked. Narrowed: any value the host's own secret store released is masked whatever its shape.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-UICHAT-7 masks on the host at render time by recognised format and by store-released value, and says 'A credential in no published format, and not held by the store, is drawn as written'. Masking by name would hide ordinary values that use the same names and would train users to ignore the masks; a string with no known format cannot be told from ordinary text.

reason: The Continue action is offered after a fixed list of six failure codes that does not follow the provider's configurable retry settings, and continuing after a closed stream may fail again.
justification: Deliberate: a manual action a person relies on must not appear or disappear when an operator tunes automatic retry, and the page says that continuing may fail again. DH-ADR-API-3 states it since the convergence round, as a recommended default: the list is fixed, independent of a provider's retry settings, and a new code joins it by a change to the specification, not by configuration. DH-D-API-5 builds it.

reason: A session's goal survives a switch to a preset that has no goal tools, and the goal strip can still edit, pause, resume or clear it; the strip now says when the current preset offers no goal tools.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words since the final re-check: DH-ADR-JOBS-9 has 'Scope boundary of this record: a goal belongs to the session, not to the agent preset that offered the goal tools, so it survives a preset switch and the host's goal service still drives, pauses and clears it; this is a product choice because the goal is state in the session's own log, and a preset only decides which tools the model sees'.

reason: A half-typed answer to a question is kept in the browser tab where it was typed; another browser or device sees the question, which is host state, but not the unsent answer.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the records' own words: DH-ADR-UICONV-7 says 'Unsent question answers are fields marked data-draft, kept by C1's per-tab store, so another browser sees the question and not the draft', and DH-ADR-REACT-1 lists unsent question answers in the small per-tab store. Saving each keystroke on the host would cost a request per pause in typing and need a merge rule for two people answering one question.

reason: The web view shows a preset but cannot create or edit one. (Removed: an override no longer replaces a preset's whole child list, and the viewer shows which layer supplied each child.)
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-UIWORK-8 states that a preset is chosen for a blank session and inspected, not edited, in this view. Authoring a preset is editing composition, which has one owner and one validation path (configuration layers and the settings forms); a second editor would be a second way to write layers.

reason: Register entry U-K2-6, resolved in the convergence round. The team view gains a read-only message timeline (DH-D-UIWORK-5): what the agents of one tree told each other, across sessions, each with sender, recipient and a link to the message. It is drawn from a new bounded query, Query.TreeMessages in session-views.md (DH-D-VIEW-5), which returns the messages of source agent-message of one tree within the caller's visibility. Tests DH-T-UIWORK-24 and DH-T-VIEW-25. A recommended default the owner has not confirmed.

From the team view a person can interrupt a running member, dismiss a settled one and manage tasks, but cannot start or rename a member, and a member's write scope in a shared checkout is a label marked 'advisory, not enforced'.
justification: Register entry U-K2-6, recorded as scope in the convergence round (a recommended default the owner has not confirmed). DH-ADR-UIWORK-5 and DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-11 state that starting and renaming stay the model's: a start needs a creator agent and its delegation bounds, and a member's name is the ledger's key for messages. Write scopes stay advisory in a shared checkout; a member that must not touch its siblings' files is started with isolation: worktree (DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-12, the owner's resolution of U-K1-3 in DH-ADR-40).

reason: In a file comparison each hunk is coloured on its own, so a line inside a comment or string that starts above the hunk can be coloured wrongly, and unknown file types stay plain. (Removed: the 5,000-line drawing cap.)
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-UIWORK-7 draws deliverables from logged facts and stored hunks and says 'Colour is computed per hunk, so a line inside a long comment or string that starts above the hunk can be coloured wrongly'; only bounded hunks are stored with the event. Colouring with full context would need the whole old and new file again. The effect is cosmetic and limited to multi-line constructs.

reason: A changed file outside the workspace is found only by the absolute path recorded at the time; after it is moved, opening the current file reports that the source is missing. Narrowed: the comparison and a presented file's kept copy no longer depend on that path.
justification: An absolute path names a place, not a file: operating systems give no portable identity that follows a file when it or its folder is moved, and a path outside the workspace has no root to be made relative to. The card states the condition instead of failing silently (DH-ADR-UIWORK-7).

reason: The directory picker lists directories and creates one; it has no search, no multi-select, no rename and no delete. A prefix filter of the listed level is kept.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the records' own words since the fix pass: DH-ADR-UISIDE-8 has 'Scope boundary of this record: the directory picker has a prefix filter and New folder, and no search, multi-select, rename or delete', and DH-ADR-HOST-8 has the same boundary for the host's browser. The dialog's job is to return one directory path; rename or delete would let a web page change the host's filesystem outside the tool pipeline, and search would walk the whole machine.

reason: Entries in the navigation column and the start page can be hidden but not reordered; they appear in the order the product declares.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words since the final re-check: DH-ADR-UISIDE-9 has 'Scope boundary of this record: entries in the navigation column and the start page can be hidden but not reordered, and appear in the order the product declares, because a second stored order for a handful of links would have to be reconciled whenever a component that contributes an entry loads or unloads'.

reason: The side panel and its More menu exist only on a session page; the navigation column's menu is available everywhere.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-UISIDE-3 makes the side panel a host-stored list of tabs that belongs to a session and says 'The panel still needs a session', and DH-ADR-API-8 addresses every file and terminal route through a session for access control. Without a session there is nothing the panel is allowed to show.

reason: The More menus do not list plugins; they hold one link that opens the plugins page.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-UISIDE-9 says what each More menu holds (the hidden entries, 'Browse plugins' and 'Create your plugin'); DH-ADR-13 gives the product no plugin discovery, and DH-ADR-UISET-5 shows what is installed, what it asked for and what it was granted in one place, the plugins page. A second list in a menu would add nothing a person can act on there.

reason: Register entry U-K2-7, resolved in the convergence round. DH-ADR-UISIDE-9 now defines 'room' against the transcript's minimum readable width (the design-system token --frame-centre-min, 400 px) and not its default width, so the session panel docks on laptop widths by narrowing the transcript and is an overlay only below that. DH-D-UIKIT-5 owns the token and the proof: test DH-T-UIKIT-12 fails a dock rule that names the default width, and scenario DH-E-UIKIT-3 expects a docked panel at 1,600 and 1,100 px and an overlay at 900 px. A recommended default the owner has not confirmed. One stale sentence remains: the tradeoff of DH-ADR-UISIDE-9 still says the panel is an overlay on laptop widths.
The sections of the session panel cannot be hidden or reordered by the user; every section with something to show is drawn, in the product's order.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words: DH-ADR-UISIDE-9 says 'Sections cannot be hidden or reordered'; it makes the panel's sections regions and spends the hidden-entry preference on the navigation column and the start page, where the lists are longer. The panel holds a few sections, each of which draws nothing when empty.

reason: The unread marker tells one person whether something finished that they have not looked at; there are no message counts and nobody sees what another person has read. (New: a non-owner gets reminders of their own.)
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-UISIDE-2 defines reading state as a stored position per person, kept 'keyed by principal and session', so each person's marker is their own and no other person's reading is stored or shown. Showing one person what another has read is a different feature with its own privacy question, and no outcome asks for it.

reason: The preview panel shows files but does not edit them and has no search of its own; a file of unknown type is shown as plain text. (Gain: host-rendered text is ordinary page content, so the browser's own find works on it.)
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words since the fix pass: DH-ADR-UISIDE-5 has 'Scope boundary of this record: a preview never edits; changing a file is the agent's tools' job or the person's own editor's'. Writing a file is the agent's work through the guarded tool pipeline, or the person's own editor and terminal; an editor in the page would be a second, unguarded way to change the workspace.

reason: How faithfully an office document is previewed, and whether missing fonts are reported (they are not for binary doc and ppt files), depends on the LibreOffice the operator installed; the preview opens no native Office application and downloads no engine.
justification: Conversion fidelity and font diagnostics are properties of LibreOffice, a third-party program, and of its version, which the preview reports but cannot improve. That LibreOffice is operator-installed, never bundled or downloaded, is owner decision DH-ADR-20.

reason: A PDF page is drawn into a bitmap of at most 16,777,216 pixels, so a very large page, or a high zoom on a dense display, looks softer than the display could show.
justification: Reclassed from platform limit in the re-sweep, and stated as a choice in the record's own words since the final re-check: DH-ADR-UISIDE-5 has 'Scope boundary of this record, PDF sharpness: each page bitmap is capped at 16,777,216 pixels; ... the cap is kept on purpose, not forced by the browser, because one such bitmap is already 64 MiB of memory in the tab and the cost grows with the square of the zoom, and drawing large pages in tiles would add a second drawing path ... for a side-panel preview whose full-quality route is Download'.

reason: An HTML preview can return to the top when it is reloaded, because the page cannot read or set the scroll position inside the sandboxed frame that shows it. (Removed: host-rendered previews, images and the PDF page and zoom keep their position.)
justification: The browser hides the inside of a frame without same-origin access from the page that embeds it, and that isolation is what keeps a previewed file from reaching the application (DH-ADR-UISIDE-5). Weakening it to restore a scroll offset would trade a security control for a convenience.

reason: A scripted HTML preview gets only the script and stylesheet files it references directly, packed by the host; the previewed page cannot read other workspace files.
justification: Deliberate security boundary, stated in the record's own words since the final re-check: DH-ADR-UISIDE-5 has 'Scope boundary of this record: a scripted HTML preview gets only the script and stylesheet files the page references directly, packed by the host, and has no bridge to the workspace, so the previewed page cannot read or list any other file, because a script in a previewed file is untrusted content and the sandboxed frame is the control' (DH-ADR-DOMPURIFY-2).

reason: The files view lists and opens files and searches names and paths; it has no search inside file contents, no artifact filter, no drag-and-drop and no rename.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-UISIDE-6 draws a read-only tree, for the reason given for the preview: a rename or a drop from a web page would change the workspace outside the tool pipeline. Content search is a tool the agent has; a person uses their editor or the terminal. Since the convergence round the tradeoff of DH-ADR-UISIDE-6 records the whole list as scope (a recommended default the owner has not confirmed).

reason: The files tree starts at the session's workspace root and cannot go above it.
justification: Deliberate, and the same boundary as unit api.workspace-files.3: DH-ADR-API-8 keeps listing, search and watching inside the workspace so that a session's file view is scoped to its project. A single named file outside the root can still be previewed when the session's filesystem backend allows the read.

reason: The page with no session selected shows nothing in the side panel.
justification: Deliberate, and the same boundary as unit client.ui-entry-customization.5: DH-ADR-UISIDE-3 keeps the side panel's tabs per session, and files, previews and terminals are reached through a session because their routes are access-controlled per session. Without a session there is no directory and no access rule to draw under.

reason: A change to the side panel's layout cannot be undone with an undo command. Upstream's hidden undo machinery is gone as well: no operation sequence is recorded.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-UISIDE-3 states that there is no dock engine and no operation log, and its tradeoff says 'no undo'. The layout is a short list of tabs in at most two panes; a closed preview is reopened from the tree or its link, and a terminal's tab cannot be lost because it is the host's roster.

reason: Starting a terminal can fail because the shell program is missing or the operating system gives no pseudo-terminal; the tab shows the error with a retry and does not start a different shell on its own.
justification: Whether a shell exists and whether a pseudo-terminal can be allocated are facts of the machine at that moment (see unit api.terminal-controller.2). Falling back silently would run the person's commands in a program they did not choose; the shell menu lets them choose another one explicitly (DH-ADR-UISIDE-7).

reason: Completion menus and inline suggestions in a terminal are whatever the user's shell provides; the web UI adds none of its own.
justification: Completion is a feature of the shell program and its configuration. A terminal's contract is that keys reach the program unmodified; a completion engine in the page would have to guess the shell's state and would compete with the shell's own.

reason: Register entry U-K2-8, resolved in the convergence round. The snapshot a terminal attachment receives gains a bounded palette section (execution.md section 6.2, DH-D-EXEC-7): the indexed, foreground, background and cursor colours a program set through escape sequences and has not reset, recorded by the host from the byte stream itself, so it does not depend on what the emulator exposes. The terminal island applies the section before it draws (DH-D-UISIDE-7), so a shell theme survives a tab switch and a reload. Tests DH-T-EXEC-12 and DH-T-UISIDE-16; scenario DH-E-UISIDE-3.

A person's terminal has bounded history, its output is not sent to the agent, a tab has no split panes of its own, and its process is not restored after a host restart. Two terminals can be shown side by side in the side panel's two panes.
justification: Deliberate, and stated for the parts a person meets: DH-ADR-API-7 says a person's terminal 'produces no session event' (so nothing reaches the model), and DH-ADR-EXEC-2 says terminals end with the host. Bounded history is the per-terminal memory limit of the execution area; the absence of split panes inside one tab is not in a record, but two terminals can stand side by side in the panel's two panes (DH-ADR-UISIDE-3).

reason: Searching the content of sessions matches literal words and phrases; a misspelt query finds nothing. (Removed: a result now opens the session at the matching event.)
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words since the final re-check: DH-ADR-VIEW-5 has 'Scope boundary of this record: session search matches exact tokens, prefixes and literal substrings, and does not tolerate typing errors; this is a product choice because stock FTS5 has no fuzzy matching, a spelling index would add a second index and a custom extension, and exact matches give results a person can predict'.

reason: Register entry U-K2-9, resolved in the convergence round. The session list and the search results are marked for the design-system area's navigable-list island (k-list, in the widget table of ui-kit.md under DH-ADR-UIKIT-3): one row is in the Tab order, Up and Down move, Home and End jump, Right and Left open and close a workspace group. Without script every row is still a native link reached by Tab (DH-D-UISIDE-1). Test DH-T-UISIDE-1 checks the marking, and scenario DH-E-UISIDE-1 walks the list with the keyboard alone.
A notice from the vendor account is shown as plain text with two actions (dismiss, open the account section), and a failed poll keeps the cards already shown.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words since the final re-check: DH-ADR-UISET-7 has 'Scope boundary of this record: a vendor account notice is shown as plain text with two actions (dismiss, and open the account section), and a failed poll keeps the cards already shown, because rendering the vendor's markup or links would mean trusting a third party's content inside an owner's page'. Notices are off by default.

reason: Automatic review can be chosen for the current session only, never as the default for new sessions, and it is offered only when the experimental review layer is loaded, behind a confirmation.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the records' own words: DH-ADR-HUMAN-6 has 'Scope boundaries of this record: ... the reserved auto preset of the experimental review layer can never be the default for new sessions, because a default must work in a composition that does not mount that layer', and DH-ADR-UISET-8 says 'auto appears only if the experimental review layer registers it'.

reason: Profile and balance are read from the vendor's web endpoints when the account panel is opened; each card can fail on its own, and usage and top-up are links to the vendor's site.
justification: The vendor offers no other interface for these facts, and what the endpoints return is the vendor's to decide. DH-ADR-HUMAN-11 and DH-ADR-UISET-7 bound the cost: nothing is fetched until the person opens the panel, no token rides on the links, and a failed query never shows a manufactured zero.

reason: Signing in to the vendor account from the web UI works only when the UI is opened at a loopback address; behind another host name or a reverse proxy the panel explains this, offers no start control, and the deployment uses an API key instead.
justification: The vendor's authorization service accepts only loopback callback origins; that list is the vendor's and cannot be changed from this side. The Go design replaces upstream's generic retry state with an explanation (DH-ADR-UISET-7).

reason: How the settings page behaves under a phone's on-screen keyboard is not validated: a phone may work, and is not tested.
justification: Register entry U-K2-10, recorded as scope in the convergence round. DH-ADR-UIKIT-3 now states a device floor as a recommended default the owner has not confirmed: desktop browsers are the supported target, narrow layouts are for narrow desktop windows, and behaviour under an on-screen keyboard is outside the guarantee. Owner decision DH-ADR-39 names the supported browsers. The risk is lower than upstream's because settings is an ordinary scrolling page.

reason: Register entry U-K2-11, resolved in the convergence round. DH-ADR-LLM-6 gives every vendor entry of the embedded catalogue a display name and optional search aliases, and test DH-T-LLM-9 fails when an entry has none. The provider picker shows the name with the route identifier as secondary text and filters on the name, the identifier and the aliases (DH-D-UISET-4, test DH-T-UISET-11). The picker was already one host-filtered search with the custom endpoint pinned.
A skill reference in a message is plain text: a name typed by hand is the same reference as one picked from the menu, and the host judges the text that was sent.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-UICHAT-2 makes a chip's identity its canonical mention text and says 'A typed or pasted token becomes a chip only when the host next renders the draft'; DH-ADR-UISET-9 says 'A reference stays text, by A14's rule' and draws a skill call from the log alone. A model request must be rebuilt from the log as it was sent, so a chip must not become a second truth beside the text.

reason: The count of local changes is computed with Git's clean and process filters skipped, so a file that Git LFS has materialised can be counted as changed although ordinary Git calls it clean. (Removed: a Git too old to honour the override is refused.)
justification: Deliberate safety rule: a filter is a program named by the repository's configuration, and running it during a background refresh would execute repository code on every tool result. DH-ADR-XFORGE-6 runs every Git command under the session's policy and, since the convergence round, states the rule and its cost in its own text: no repository-configured program runs and nothing is fetched implicitly when the harness inspects or creates a checkout. The panel marks the count 'filters skipped'.

reason: The status of a pull request is refreshed only while a browser tab shows that session's panel, and nothing notifies the user when checks finish meanwhile; a session-list row shows the stored status with its age.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XFORGE-3 contacts a code host only while someone is looking and states the tradeoff: 'No notification when checks finish while no panel is open; a list row can be stale and says how old it is'. Polling with no viewer would contact the user's code host in the background and spend the user's rate limit with nobody to show the result to.

reason: A change made to working files outside the session shows in the panel only at the next trigger (a tool result, a panel fetch or a refresh, at most once per 10 seconds). Narrowed: a commit or a branch switch made outside appears promptly through a watch on the Git HEAD file.
justification: Deliberate cost choice: watching a whole working tree would cost one watch per directory of every open session's repository, for a panel that is a status summary. DH-ADR-XFORGE-9 (item a), added in the convergence round as a recommended default, records 'seen at the next trigger, not watched' as scope and says what would reopen it; DH-D-XFORGE-6 builds the triggers.

reason: Restoring a worktree whose directory was removed recreates it from its branch, or from the commit the branch started from; changes that were never committed are lost, and an existing or incomplete directory blocks the restore.
justification: Git holds only what was committed, so nothing can bring back files that existed only in the removed directory. The card says so before the user chooses Restore, and DH-ADR-XFORGE-7 never overwrites an existing directory.

reason: The model has no dedicated tool for the pull requests bound to its session; it reads and changes them by running gh or glab through the shell tool.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XFORGE-1 makes the forge seam read-only and states that a change to a code host is made by the model's own command in the shell tool, which is sandboxed and guarded. A host-side tool would act with the user's own sign-in outside the session's sandbox and network policy. The owner confirmed the boundary: the code-host UI is status only, with no host-side writes (DH-ADR-38).

reason: GitHub status needs the gh program installed and signed in on the host for each listed host; tokens in environment variables are not used and an unlisted host is never read. Without gh the cards say unavailable with the reason.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XFORGE-2 has providers drive the operator-installed vendor program ('No token is read, stored or passed; the CLI uses its own credential store'), and DH-ADR-XFORGE-3 contacts 'only a listed host'.

reason: The number of unresolved review threads on a pull request is counted up to a configured maximum; beyond it the card shows a lower bound marked N+.
justification: GitHub's interface offers no count of unresolved threads, so a provider must page through them, and an unbounded page loop would let one pull request exhaust the user's rate limit. The bound is configuration. (The review read upstream also mentions is not built.)

reason: A pull request whose head branch lives in a fork is not found by branch name; it appears when the session's own create command prints its address, or when the user adds it by link.
justification: Deliberate deferral: discovering it needs a lookup of the fork's parent on every push, and a branch name in a fork can collide with someone else's pull request, which the 'never guess' rule of DH-ADR-XFORGE-4 forbids. DH-ADR-XFORGE-9 (item b), added in the convergence round as a recommended default, records it as scope: a head lookup qualified by the fork's owner would reopen it.

reason: Every status poll costs at least one GitHub query, counted against the signed-in account's rate limit. (Removed: the queries for diffs, review reads and review writes, which are not built.)
justification: GitHub meters its interface per account and offers a local tool no push channel, so status is read by polling. DH-ADR-XFORGE-3 bounds the cost: polling only while a panel is shown, at upstream's cadence, backing off until the reset time on a rate-limited answer.

reason: GitLab status needs the glab program installed and signed in for each listed host; an unlisted host is never read, and a host whose SSH remotes use another name, or a GitLab installed under a path prefix, is not recognised.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XFORGE-2 (the harness holds no forge token) and DH-ADR-XFORGE-3 (only a listed host is contacted). Recognising hosts by anything but the listed names would guess at where the user's credentials may be sent.

reason: The merge-request card shows only what GitLab Community Edition reports; required approvals, code owners and merged-results pipelines of the paid tiers are not shown.
justification: Deliberate deferral: a query that names a paid-tier field is refused by a Community Edition host, so reading those fields needs a capability probe per host and a second query shape. DH-ADR-XFORGE-9 (item c), added in the convergence round as a recommended default, records it as scope: a test installation on a paid tier would reopen it.

reason: Every status poll costs one GitLab query per batch plus one request per merge request whose mergeability must be rechecked. (Removed: the requests for review reads, diff versions, draft notes and writes, which are not built.)
justification: GitLab meters its interface and rechecks mergeability only when a REST read asks for it; a local tool gets no push channel. The cost is bounded by polling only while a panel is shown (DH-ADR-XFORGE-3) and by the configured batch size and concurrency.

reason: A pull request is linked to a session only when a recognised command (one with a compiled-in rule) names it plainly; commands that use shell expansion, substitutions, multi-line scripts, aliases or a bare number without a repository do not link.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XFORGE-4 states that rules never guess and never execute, so a binding is always a fact. Misses are recovered by branch discovery after a push or on inspection, and by Add by link in the panel.

reason: A pull request that someone opened elsewhere for a branch appears only after the next push of that branch, the next inspection that reports the branch, or a manual add.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XFORGE-3 says 'a request is made in three cases only: a tab is showing that session's panel, the user pressed refresh, or the session pushed a branch (one lookup)', so a pull request opened elsewhere is learned of only then; DH-ADR-JOBS-12 defers event-triggered automation. The registry keeps one refresh entry that an intake component could call later.

reason: The model cannot read or change the list of pull requests bound to its session through a tool.
justification: Deliberate, and the same boundary as unit forge-bundle.2: DH-ADR-XFORGE-1 keeps the forge seam read-only and host-side, and DH-ADR-XFORGE-4 writes bindings only from settled shell calls. A host-side forge tool would act with the user's sign-in outside the session's sandbox.

reason: Register entry U-K2-12, resolved in the convergence round. The binding listener also reads the durable record the jobs area writes when a job settles, for jobs a shell tool call started, and scans the job's output with the same rules and the same byte bound (DH-D-XFORGE-5). The jobs area states what that needs: the job/settled record names the originating tool call and its command, and the output is still readable when subscribers are told (jobs-schedule-goal-plan.md, persisted data; DH-D-JOBS-2). Test DH-T-XFORGE-10 covers a settled background job and the case where the record lacks the call or the output is gone, which binds nothing.
Pull-request status reaches the UI on the next poll or when the user presses refresh; a code host cannot push a change to the harness.
justification: Deliberate, and the same boundary as unit forge-session.3: DH-ADR-XFORGE-3 says a request is made in three cases only (a panel is shown, the user pressed refresh, the session pushed a branch), and DH-ADR-JOBS-12 defers event-triggered automation. A code host can deliver a webhook only to an address it can reach, which a harness on a loopback address is not.

reason: The model's worktree tools create, enter and leave a worktree; they do not list, merge or remove one, and enter reaches only the worktrees of the checkout the session is in.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XFORGE-8 says worktrees are 'created explicitly, before the first turn or by the tool'; DH-ADR-XFORGE-6 says 'enter_worktree accepts a target only if it lies inside the session's current write roots' and that only a person can move a session elsewhere; DH-ADR-XFORGE-7 says cleanup 'never deletes a branch'. Removal and merge destroy or rewrite work, and the model already has git through the sandboxed shell tool for them. No record says in so many words that the tools do not list or merge.

reason: A session can enter only a registered worktree inside the configured pool of the checkout it works in, and only one inside its current write roots.
justification: Deliberate, and tightened: DH-ADR-XFORGE-6 states that a worktree move never widens what a session may write, so a name chosen by the model cannot move the session, and with it the write boundary, to an arbitrary directory.

reason: Leaving a worktree keeps its branch and files, and cleanup never deletes a branch, so branches accumulate until the user deletes them. Narrowed: a failed setup is rolled back, and what a crash leaves behind is recorded in a journal row and reported.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XFORGE-7 removes only clean, unreferenced checkouts and never a branch, because a branch holds commits, which are the user's work, and a checkout with uncommitted files must never be removed by the harness. The decision names the accumulating branches as its tradeoff.

reason: Creating a worktree fetches only the one remote branch a request names; it does not fetch other commits, initialise submodules, install dependencies or copy uncommitted files.
justification: Deliberate: an explicit pinned baseline with no implicit network use and no repository code run during creation (the rule kept under DH-ADR-XFORGE-6, where every Git command runs under the session's policy). Submodules and dependencies are steps the agent runs through the sandboxed shell. Since the convergence round DH-ADR-XFORGE-6 states it in its own text: nothing is fetched implicitly, and only the one named branch is fetched when a fetch was asked for.

reason: A new worktree is checked out with Git's filters skipped, so Git LFS files stay pointers and encrypted files stay encrypted until the user or the agent hydrates them deliberately.
justification: Deliberate safety rule, the same as unit client-ui-forge.1: a filter is a program named by the repository's configuration, and running it during creation would execute repository code and may download. Since the convergence round DH-ADR-XFORGE-6 states the rule and its cost in its own text: clean, smudge and process filters are switched off for the call, so a file kept by Git LFS stays a pointer in a new worktree.

reason: A person watching a shared session has no file preview and no terminal. (Removed: no installed-plugin method is exposed to a viewer.)
justification: Deliberate, and decided by the owner (DH-ADR-37: no relay, and viewers only watch): DH-ADR-XSHARE-3 says 'One role, four read actions' and that a viewer watches and cannot act. The file routes can read any file the session's filesystem backend allows and a terminal is command execution as the operating-system user; neither can be made safe for a second person by a role alone.

reason: The statistics view is not part of the default product; the operator enables the developer-tools bundle with one switch. (Removed: there is nothing to install, the view is compiled into the one binary.)
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-BUNDLE-1 says 'Experimental features are optional bundles, each one disabled group', and DH-ADR-BUNDLE-10 requires every catalogue component to be mounted by a shipped layer or to be on the optional list. Promotion to the default product is a later owner decision.

reason: The timing figures are computed from the session log, not measured by a sampler: total time is last step end minus first step start, and waiting in queues lands in a segment called rest. Improved: first-token and model time are recorded on each attempt event.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XINSPECT-4 says in its title that the statistics are 'host pages over Query and one fold', with stepStats a row projection, so there is no sampler and no second source of numbers that could disagree with the log (DH-ADR-PERSISTENCE-7).

reason: A file that the chat export does not contain (every non-image file and some images) cannot be opened after import; it becomes a text note with its name and size. (Changed: no file handle points the model at an empty path.)
justification: The bytes are not in the vendor's export file, so no importer can restore them. DH-D-XINSPECT-7 builds the note form.

reason: The chat importer leaves out other branches of a conversation, content-filtered rounds, risk disclaimers, tips, page-find and partial-read records, encrypted link bodies, the pinned flag, per-token times and accumulated token usage.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words since the final re-check: DH-ADR-XINSPECT-7 has 'Scope boundary of this record: the chat importer keeps one branch of each conversation and leaves out the other branches, content-filtered rounds, risk disclaimers, tips, page-find and partial-read records, encrypted link bodies, the pinned flag, per-token times and accumulated token usage, because a session is a linear log and the dropped records are either never shown as reply text by the vendor's site or must not enter the model's context'.

reason: The chat importer targets one structure of the vendor's export format (version 3 as of 2026-11-12); it refuses another version and skips record types it does not know.
