justification: The format belongs to the vendor's website, is not specified for third parties and can change without notice; supporting generations nobody can test would be a claim without evidence. DH-D-XINSPECT-7 builds the version check and the per-conversation skip with a coded reason.

reason: Every task update writes the whole current task tree to the session log as one event, bounded by the session's event size limit and a maximum number of tasks.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words: DH-ADR-XINSPECT-5 names 'a whole tree per task update (kept on purpose)' in its tradeoff, because a state-carrying session event holds the whole new value so that the latest event alone restores the state (DH-ADR-PERSISTENCE-7). The bound replaces upstream's separate 2 MiB figure.

reason: Pause and Continue on the timeline are requests: they reach the agent as a notice and take effect when the model updates its plan. Stopping a running turn is the separate Stop control, shown beside them.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words since the final re-check: DH-ADR-XINSPECT-5 has 'Scope boundary of this record: Pause and Continue on the timeline are requests that reach the agent as a notice and take effect when the model records them in its plan, and stopping a running turn is the loop's own cancel (DH-ADR-ARCH-3) shown as the separate Stop control, because a panel click must never abort a tool call in flight'.

reason: Dictation takes one complete recording and returns text; there is no audio file upload, no stored history of transcripts and no streaming. (Removed: the recording is sent as plain audio, not base64.)
justification: Deliberate, and every clause is now stated in the record's own words: DH-ADR-XCUA-5 says 'There is no automatic send, no always-on microphone and no streaming' and has 'Scope boundary of this record: dictation takes one complete recording and returns text, with no audio file upload and no stored history of transcripts, because a history would keep speech the user never chose to send, and an uploaded file is an attachment, not dictation'.

reason: Browser use drives Chromium-family browsers only; Firefox and WebKit cannot be selected.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words: DH-ADR-XCUA-2 ships one browser provider, chromedp speaking the Chrome DevTools Protocol to an installed Chrome, and its tradeoff says 'Chromium family only'; DH-ADR-XCUA-3 admits the two Node servers only as optional recipes configured for Chromium. The browser seam admits another provider later without changing the model's tools.

reason: When the harness attaches to a browser the user already runs, the user and other programs can still change the same pages; the harness's reservation only keeps its own sessions apart.
justification: An attached browser is the user's own program and its debugging interface accepts any client; nothing the harness holds can lock the user out of their browser. The design narrows the exposure: launching a private browser is the default, attach needs an approval (DH-ADR-MEDIA-5), and the optional Node recipes do not offer attach.

reason: Cancelling a browser action cannot undo a navigation or a click the browser already received.
justification: A real browser has no undo for delivered input; this is true of every provider. The result says that the outcome is unknown and tells the model to look before retrying; nothing is replayed.

reason: Browser use through the optional Playwright recipe drives Chromium-family browsers only.
justification: Deliberate, and the same boundary as unit browser-use-chrome-devtools-mcp.1: DH-ADR-XCUA-2 says 'Chromium family only', and DH-ADR-XCUA-3 admits the Node servers as optional recipes in launch mode only.

reason: An attached browser can still be changed by its user and by other programs; the reservation keeps only harness sessions apart.
justification: The same fact as unit browser-use-chrome-devtools-mcp.3: an attached browser is the user's own. Launching a private browser is the default, attach needs an approval (DH-ADR-MEDIA-5), and the optional Node recipes do not offer attach at all.

reason: Cancelling a browser action cannot undo a navigation or a click the browser already received.
justification: The same fact as unit browser-use-chrome-devtools-mcp.5: a real browser has no undo for delivered input. The result reports an unknown outcome and nothing is replayed.

reason: Exclusive use of an attached browser holds inside one host process only; another harness process, another program or the user can act in the same browser.
justification: An attached browser is owned by its user, and a reservation shared between processes would still not stop the user or another program from acting in it. The design relies on launching a private browser by default and an approval before the first use of an attached one (DH-ADR-MEDIA-5).

reason: Cancelling or losing the connection cannot undo browser actions already delivered. (Removed for a launched browser: an operation that ignores cancellation can no longer delay cleanup without limit, because the browser's process tree is stopped by a bounded ladder.)
justification: Undoing delivered input is impossible for any provider. The result reports an unknown outcome and nothing is replayed.

reason: The bullet describes the Stagehand provider, which the Go design does not build: owner decision DH-ADR-24 drops the Stagehand browser layer and DH-ADR-XCUA-2 drops the provider whole. The Chromium-only boundary of the provider that is built is carried under unit browser-use-chrome-devtools-mcp.1.

A resumed or forked session gets its recorded conversation back, but not the browser: pages, cookies and logins from before are gone. The Stagehand provider this bullet was written for is dropped (DH-ADR-24); the limit is kept here because it holds for the provider that replaces it.
justification: A live browser process cannot be rebuilt from a log. The browser service records browser state events, so the first browser result after a resume says that earlier pages and logins are gone.

reason: The bullet describes the Stagehand provider, which the Go design does not build (owner decision DH-ADR-24; DH-ADR-XCUA-2 drops the provider whole). The same fact for the providers that are built, that an attached browser can also be changed by its user, is carried under units browser-use-chrome-devtools-mcp.3 and browser-use-runtime.2.

Voice input never sends a message by itself and has no always-on microphone, wake word, live captions or spoken replies; and local recognition means the machine that runs the host, which may not be the machine with the browser.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XCUA-5 says 'There is no automatic send, no always-on microphone and no streaming' and that insertion happens only into an unchanged draft or on an explicit click; DH-ADR-XCUA-4 says 'the host runs an operator-installed recognition program as a child process', which is why local means the host's machine. No record names spoken replies; the area's limits list does. The settings page states where each provider processes audio.

reason: Computer use works only after the operator installed a driver and granted it the operating system's permissions by hand; enabling the entry does not prove that every desktop action is permitted.
justification: Deliberate: owner decision DH-ADR-19 says 'The Go project ships no native helper. Computer use works only when the operator installs an external MCP server that provides it', so installation and the system permissions are the operator's steps. The adapter reads the driver's permission status at start-up without prompting and shows it before the first call.

reason: Installing software grants no desktop access and creates no graphical session: computer use needs a logged-in, unlocked desktop and permissions granted by hand.
justification: Operating systems tie desktop-control permissions to a user's explicit grant and need a graphical session to observe or send input; no program can grant them to itself. They are listed as the operator's steps, and the status view shows the driver's permission state (DH-ADR-19).

reason: The user and programs other than the harness can change the same desktop between two computer-use calls.
justification: A desktop cannot be reserved against its own user. What the design adds is a turn-length lease between harness sessions (DH-ADR-MEDIA-6: one session at a time) and the rule that every reference is checked against the latest observation.

reason: A cancelled computer-use call may already have delivered its input, and nothing on the desktop is rolled back.
justification: Synthetic input, once delivered to an application, cannot be taken back by any driver. The result says the outcome is unknown and tells the model to observe before retrying; no call is replayed.

reason: On macOS the system permissions for desktop control need the user's approval in System Settings; enabling computer use in the harness grants none.
justification: macOS ties a privacy permission to a program's identity and to the user's own approval. With DH-ADR-19 the permission belongs to the driver's application, the harness never requests it, and the status view shows whether it is present.

reason: Input sent by computer use can fail to take effect in some applications; a successful result confirms that the input was delivered, not that it worked.
justification: Applications decide how they treat synthetic input, and some ignore it; this is a property of desktop automation and of whichever driver the operator installed. The contract is that a result reports delivery and never effect, and the model observes after acting.

reason: The application a session grant names is identified only as well as the operating system and the driver expose it: a stable identifier where the driver's listing has one, otherwise the process id, in which case the grant ends when the application exits.
justification: The harness ships no native code and does not inspect applications itself (DH-ADR-19); the identity comes from the third-party driver and from what the operating system exposes for a running program. The fallback fails closed and costs one more prompt.

reason: The planned evidence proves the computer-use contract with a replayed model on one test application; whether a real model completes real desktop tasks is not measured. (Upstream's first sentence, about program execution and retained state, no longer applies.)
justification: Deliberate scope of evidence, stated in the record's own words since the final re-check: DH-ADR-XCUA-1 has 'Scope boundary of this record: the evidence proves the computer-use contract (the action mapping, the approval path, the results and the cleanup) with a replayed model on one test application, and does not measure whether a real model completes real desktop tasks, because task success is a property of the chosen model and of a driver and applications the project neither ships nor pins'.

reason: A reference to an on-screen element is valid only until the next observation of its window, and a screenshot or pointer action must name a window.
justification: An accessibility tree is a snapshot: the operating system gives no element identity that survives the next read, and an old identifier may be reused for another control. The contract therefore makes a stale reference an error and never a guess (DH-ADR-MEDIA-6).

reason: Pointer coordinates are pixels of the last screenshot of a window, and the window can move or change between the screenshot and the input. (The relative 0 to 999 mode is not offered.)
justification: On a desktop shared with its user, nothing can freeze a window between an observation and an input. The adapter scales a point by the stored image size so that the model does no arithmetic, and a changed window is reported as an error (DH-ADR-XCUA-1).

reason: A window-manager feature that shrinks background windows to thumbnails (macOS Stage Manager) can defeat observation and pointer input for a background window.
justification: Operating-system behaviour that no harness code can change, and now the installed driver's to handle (DH-ADR-19). The driver's degraded flag is passed to the model, and the adapter never forces a window to the foreground.

reason: There is no Always allow for an application: a grant lasts until the session ends, and another session needs its own consent.
justification: Deliberate: owner decision DH-ADR-16 says 'Grants are logged, listed and revocable, and never outlive the session. No rules are stored across sessions', and DH-ADR-33 confirms that a grant names one application and is never copied. The Go design adds the session grant itself, which upstream's Windows provider lacked.

reason: On Windows, computer-use input may move the user's real mouse pointer, depending on the installed driver; the harness cannot prevent it or ask separately for it.
justification: How input reaches a Windows application is the behaviour of the third-party driver and of the operating system's input model (DH-ADR-19). The adapter always requests background delivery (DH-ADR-XCUA-1) but cannot enforce it; the real-desktop scenario records whether the pointer moved.

reason: The model cannot find or start an application through computer use on any platform; the user opens the application.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XCUA-1 exposes the driver through an allow-list of tools and says 'Hover, drag, held keys, launching an application and foreground delivery are unavailable', and DH-ADR-MEDIA-6 approves computer use per application; a grant names a running application, and launching one is an action outside any grant.

reason: Computer use needs an unlocked, interactive desktop session, and a window that is listed can still be unavailable for capture or input.
justification: An operating-system fact: a locked or non-interactive session has no desktop to capture or send input to, and capture support is decided per window by the system. It is listed as an operator prerequisite, and the driver's error is returned as a computer-use error result.

reason: Which applications and inputs work, and how well that was validated, is owned by the installed driver and its vendor, not by the harness.
justification: Deliberate: owner decision DH-ADR-19 makes an external MCP server the only route to computer use, and DH-ADR-XCUA-1 says 'the project neither pins nor audits the driver'. The harness validates one driver version on one test application in its real-desktop scenario, records that version, and claims no coverage of other applications.

reason: The user and other programs can change an application between two computer-use calls, and the mouse pointer is not put back where it was.
justification: A desktop cannot be reserved against its own user, and restoring the pointer would dismiss what a hover revealed. Between harness sessions the turn-length desktop lease gives the reservation upstream declined to build (DH-ADR-MEDIA-6).

reason: Element references are opaque strings valid until the next observation; an old string may later name a different control, so callers must use references from the latest observation, and screenshots and pointer input need a named window.
justification: The same fact as unit cua-macos.5: an accessibility tree is a snapshot and the operating system gives no lasting element identity. The contract makes a stale reference an error and never a guess (DH-ADR-MEDIA-6).

reason: Speech recognition transcribes complete recordings only; there is no streaming recognition and no speech synthesis.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XCUA-5 says 'no streaming' and limits voice to text proposed for the draft; DH-ADR-XCUA-4 recognises on the host with an operator-installed program that 'reads one WAV file and prints text'. Streaming needs partial-result revision and turn arbitration that dictation does not. No record names speech synthesis; nothing in the product speaks.

reason: Automatic review is a default-off optional component: no default profile, general setting or new-session default selects it; the user enables it and then chooses it for one session.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XHOOKS-4 keeps auto review as an optional policy listener, and DH-ADR-HUMAN-6 says 'the reserved auto preset of the experimental review layer can never be the default for new sessions'. The reviewer is a fallible model that lets calls run with full access, so making it reachable without an explicit choice would widen every installation.

reason: Under automatic review commands run with full access and no file sandbox, and what a script does directly is judged from its visible text only. Narrowed: the script's tool calls, made through the tool command line, are each reviewed.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words: DH-ADR-XHOOKS-4 says 'an allowed call runs with full access, and what a script does beyond its visible text is not reviewed'; owner decision DH-ADR-8 makes a script an ordinary process whose direct effects are not tool calls, a tradeoff that decision names. No per-effect review point exists.

reason: The reviewing model can misjudge a call, and there are no tool exemptions, no configurable review policy and no second attempt at a verdict. Two deterministic layers remain around it: deny-only guards still run after an allow, and under the ask policy a denial reaches a person.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XHOOKS-4 ports 'a fixed policy' and says 'The reviewer is a fallible model, not a boundary'; exemptions or a configurable policy would lower the ceiling. The limit is stated to the user when the preset is selected.

reason: A child agent run by another vendor's product (Claude Code, Codex, an OAR runtime) keeps that product's own permission system once the delegation call was allowed; automatic review does not reach inside it.
justification: Reclassed from platform limit in the re-sweep: some of these products offer a channel for permission prompts (the audit names one for Claude Code), so routing them to the reviewer is a design choice not taken, not an impossibility. The records state the choice: DH-ADR-XHOOKS-4 says 'Foreign agents started by delegation keep their own permission systems', and DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-7 runs external products in an operator-fixed mode and asks a person only where the product's protocol has an answer channel. The delegation call itself is reviewed.

reason: A hook cannot rewrite a tool call's arguments: an updatedInput field in a hook's answer is never applied, and the Go types have no place for it.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words: DH-ADR-XHOOKS-1 says 'A hook cannot allow, cannot change arguments, content or values', and outcome DH-O-6 requires that logged arguments are never rewritten. A hook that wants a different call denies with a message and the model retries. A test checks that logged arguments are byte-identical after a hook returned updatedInput.

reason: Only hooks that run a command are executed; http, mcp_tool, prompt and agent hooks are listed in the diagnostics and skipped.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XHOOKS-1 says 'Only command handlers run' and that http, mcp_tool, prompt and agent handlers 'are listed and skipped'. An http hook would send event data off the machine without an opt-in (DH-ADR-9), and prompt and agent hooks are model calls outside the session log.

reason: Of Claude Code's 30 hook events, 21 are not offered (narrowed from 23); a configured hook for one of them is listed in the diagnostics instead of being silently ignored.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XHOOKS-1 runs hooks 'at nine points' and maps each answer onto a closed set of decisions, so the other events are not offered; it is a compatibility adapter for a third-party contract that keeps growing and not a reimplementation of Claude Code. Each remaining event needs a seam another area owns or has no counterpart in this product.

reason: A SessionStart hook can add context but cannot start a turn, rename the session, set watch paths, reload skills or change the environment of later commands. (Fixed: its context is in the first request, plain output is accepted, the payload carries the model.)
justification: Deliberate: the remaining fields are outside the closed set of answers a hook may give under DH-ADR-XHOOKS-1.

reason: A UserPromptSubmit hook can reject a prompt or add context but cannot rename the session or hide or replace what the user typed. (Fixed: plain output is accepted and the default timeout is 30 seconds.)
justification: Deliberate: hiding or replacing the user's prompt would be a rewrite of what the person typed, which is outside the closed answers of DH-ADR-XHOOKS-1.

reason: A PreToolUse hook can deny or ask, but its allow never pre-approves a call, defer is not offered and it cannot rewrite the arguments. (Fixed: its added context is delivered with the same call's result.)
justification: Deliberate: under DH-ADR-XHOOKS-1 a hook's answer can only restrict. Letting an external program return allow would skip the policy listeners, guards and approval behind it, and a rewrite would break the rule that logged arguments stay as written (DH-O-6).

reason: A PostToolUse hook can block with feedback or add context but cannot replace a tool's output. (Fixed: the hook receives the rendered text and the structured value.)
justification: Deliberate: replacing a tool's content from an external program is outside the closed answers of DH-ADR-XHOOKS-1; the result the model sees stays the tool's own or a logged block.

reason: A SubagentStart hook's context reaches a child inside the harness only, not a child run by another vendor's product, and a SubagentStop hook only observes. (Fixed: the payload names the real provider, the creator's session and the child's last answer.)
justification: Deliberate for the stop hook: DH-ADR-XHOOKS-1 lists the closed set of answers (Deny or Ask before a tool, Block after it, Reject of a prompt, KeepOpen at the stop, added context, a halt), and blocking a child's settlement is not among them, because a child's result is settled by the subagent lifecycle. For an external child there is nothing to inject into: it is another vendor's process with no inbox.

reason: A hook's suppressOutput and terminalSequence flags are not applied, and transcript_path is empty unless the hook source opts in to an export file. (Fixed: payloads carry the turn id, preset, model and effort; systemMessage is shown; continue false halts the turn.)
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words since the final re-check: DH-ADR-XHOOKS-2 has 'Scope boundary of this record, Claude Code's fields: a hook's suppressOutput and terminalSequence flags are not applied, because they address a terminal interface this product does not have, and transcript_path is empty unless the hook source sets transcript: true, because the session lives in a database (DH-ADR-PERSISTENCE-3) and writing an export file on every hook run is a cost and a copy of private data that each source must opt in to'.

reason: Only command hooks run, and the options async, asyncRewake, if, once and statusMessage are not honoured. (Fixed: argument-list and shell options, concurrent matched hooks, several sources, per-session project files behind a trust digest, re-read on change.)
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XHOOKS-1 excludes non-command handlers, and an asynchronous hook would answer after the decision it was asked about; the other options belong to Claude Code's own interface. DH-ADR-XHOOKS-2 covers how a source is trusted.

reason: Of Codex's 10 hook events, PermissionRequest, PreCompact and PostCompact are not offered (narrowed from five); a configured hook for one is listed in the diagnostics, not silently dropped.
justification: Deliberate: under DH-ADR-XHOOKS-1 a hook has a closed set of answers. A permission-request hook would let an external program take part in an approval, which only an owner's answerer may settle (DH-ADR-SECURITY-5), and the compaction points belong to another area's transaction.

reason: A Codex PreToolUse hook can block, but its allow pre-approves nothing and it cannot rewrite the arguments. (Fixed: the hook sees the call's full argument object, and its added context is delivered with the call's result.)
justification: Deliberate: a hook's answer can only restrict (DH-ADR-XHOOKS-1) and logged arguments are never rewritten (DH-O-6).

reason: Only synchronous command hooks run, hooks written inline in Codex's config.toml are not read, and statusMessage and commandWindows are ignored. (Fixed: several sources, per-session project files behind a trust digest, concurrent matched hooks.)
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words since the fix pass: DH-ADR-XHOOKS-2 has 'Scope boundary of this record: a hook source is the JSON hook file both products share, at a path the operator names; hooks written inline in Codex's config.toml are not read, only synchronous command handlers run (an asynchronous hook cannot answer the decision it was asked), and Codex's statusMessage and commandWindows fields are ignored'.

reason: Only one external agent runtime is exercised by the planned real-environment scenario; the five runtimes upstream never verified (antigravity, grok, kimi, opencode, pi) can be selected, but nobody has shown that they work through the bridge.
justification: Deliberate scope of evidence: owner decision DH-ADR-23 keeps the bridge and asks for a scenario against one real installed runtime, and DH-ADR-OAR-1 says 'Five of the seven runtimes were never verified upstream and are not verified here'. Verifying a runtime needs that vendor's program and an account. DH-ADR-XHOOKS-7 gives every registered runtime the same host-owned bridge and states which were verified with which OAR version.

reason: The harness does not install, sign in to or upgrade an external agent runtime. Narrowed: what is missing (Node, the OAR package, the native agent, a version outside the range) is reported before any task text is sent and never fails host start-up.
justification: Deliberate: owner decision DH-ADR-23 keeps a path to external runtimes; DH-ADR-OAR-1 lists Node, the OAR package and each native agent as prerequisites and says 'The harness installs none of these'; DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-7 runs external products as operator-installed programs.

reason: An external agent runs under its own permission mode with no approval prompt from the harness; if it asks for an approval or for input, the run ends instead of waiting.
justification: Reclassed from platform limit in the re-sweep: the bridge does receive the native agent's request (message request in DH-ADR-OAR-1), so whether a person could answer it through OAR is unverified, not shown impossible. The records state the choice: DH-ADR-OAR-1 says 'The host answers by ending the run' and that the bridge refuses an instance that does not state its permission posture; DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-7 says a person is asked only where the product's protocol has an answer channel and every instance has a time limit.

reason: An external agent applies its own permission mode instead of the harness sandbox (the record says so), and it may keep transcripts of its own. (Fixed: the harness owns the bridge's process tree and ends it on cancel, time limit, a failed start and disposal.)
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-7 runs external products as operator-installed programs in an operator-fixed mode, because a native agent needs the network and its own sign-in files, and its history belongs to the user's installation of that product. Whether an external agent can also run inside the harness sandbox is recorded as open in subagent-team.md section 10: it can only be learned by running each product.

reason: A task given to an external agent is one prompt and one answer: no follow-up, no resume, and no rollback of files the agent changed. (Narrowed: a structured answer can be requested and progress can be shown.)
justification: Reclassed from platform limit in the re-sweep: the one-shot contract is a choice, stated by DH-ADR-OAR-1 ('Keep the provider, its one-shot contract'), made because one prompt and a wait for the turn's end is the only use of OAR for which upstream holds evidence. That changes by another vendor's agent cannot be undone by the harness is a fact; a child that must not touch the user's checkout can be isolated with isolation: worktree (DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-12).

reason: Once a person has typed into a terminal the agent opened, the agent cannot type into it again; it can read it and open a new one.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XHOOKS-8 states that control passes to the person and 'There is no hand-back'. After a person typed, the shell may hold a sudo or ssh sign-in; handing input back would give the model that authority with no approval.

reason: A command in an agent's persistent terminal runs under the policy the shell was started with and cannot ask for more access; a command that needs more is rerun with the one-shot shell tool, which can ask.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XHOOKS-8 says 'Commands inside cannot request escalation'; an approval covers one call (DH-ADR-16) and a persistent shell has one launch plan for its whole life, so widening a running shell would turn one approval into a standing one.

reason: Whether a program in a terminal has finished or is waiting for input is sometimes a guess: exact at the shell prompt on Linux and macOS, provable for a program waiting for input on Linux only, and otherwise reported as inferred from silence, with the reason.
justification: A terminal never says done; only the operating system can show that a foreign program is blocked reading the terminal, and macOS and Windows do not expose it. The execution area's readiness tiers state which answer is exact and which is inferred.

reason: When the model reads a person's terminal it gets the screen as it is at that moment; the read never waits for new output.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words since the fix pass: DH-ADR-XHOOKS-8 has 'Scope boundary of this record: a read of a person's terminal returns the screen as it is at that moment and does not wait for the program to become idle or for new output'. A waiting read would tie a tool call to the person's own work and keep reading what they type next.

reason: A ralph loop ends when the worker says the objective is complete (or a bound is hit); no independent evaluator checks the claim. The result labels the status as worker-reported and names which bound ended the run.
justification: Deliberate: an evaluator needs its own inputs, tools, checks and authority, which upstream left undefined; adding one would be a new feature. Since the convergence round the tradeoff of DH-ADR-XHOOKS-6 records it as scope (a recommended default the owner has not confirmed): ralph has no evaluator, as DH-ADR-JOBS-10 records for goals; the bound on rounds and the person reading the result are the control.

reason: A ralph run is foreground only: the tool call blocks until the run ends, with no job id, no resume after a process restart and no scheduler.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XHOOKS-6 allows the tool only in a human turn, makes it neither a workflow nor a goal, and says 'a run still blocks its tool call'. A background loop would outlive the turn that authorised it and spend tokens with nobody watching; background delegation is what a workflow job is for.

reason: Between rounds of a ralph loop the only memory is the workspace and one bounded report; each round's conversation is discarded.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XHOOKS-6 calls Start 'once per round with an output schema for the report' and 'disposes each activation before the next'. A fresh context per round is the purpose of the tool; carrying conversation across rounds would make it a goal, which the jobs area owns.

reason: One round of a ralph loop is one fresh child from one provider the operator chose; there is no fan-out inside a round and the model does not pick the provider.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XHOOKS-6 makes ralph one Start per round on the subagent seam, so there is no fan-out inside a round; that the provider is the operator's choice is in the area's configuration, not the record. Fan-out and routing are what workflows and the delegation tool are for.

reason: Delegation to an external runtime is one-shot: no follow-up or resume, and the model cannot override the runtime's permission mode per call. (Narrowed: a structured answer can be requested.)
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-OAR-1 keeps 'its one-shot contract', DH-ADR-XHOOKS-7 makes the selector the shared delegation tool, and DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-7 says 'The permission mode is part of the instance configuration; no tool argument reaches it', so a model cannot widen another vendor's agent.

reason: GitHub gets its 202 answer before any rule runs or any session exists, so GitHub learns nothing about the work that follows. Narrowed: a delivery record keyed by GitHub's delivery id names the sessions created or the failure.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-WIRE-12 has a webhook verify the raw body and answer 202; holding the provider's request open for rule and session work would tie an internet-facing connection to model activity (DH-ADR-XHOOKS-5).

reason: The GitHub webhook endpoint accepts JSON bodies only; a form-encoded delivery is refused with status 415.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words since the final re-check: DH-ADR-XHOOKS-5 has 'Scope boundary of this record: the GitHub endpoint accepts application/json bodies only and answers a form-encoded delivery with status 415, because GitHub lets the operator choose JSON, and one content type keeps this internet-facing handler to one decoder that runs only after the signature over the raw body was verified'.

reason: The webhook runtime has no queue and replays nothing by itself: after a crash a delivery is run again only when the provider redelivers it. Narrowed: a delivery is recorded before the 202 answer, and a redelivery of an unfinished or failed record runs the rules again.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-WIRE-12 keeps the runtime fire-and-forget, and DH-ADR-XHOOKS-5 says 'There is still no queue and no completion report: the provider's redelivery is the retry'; and an automatic replay could start unattended work the operator no longer wants (DH-ADR-XHOOKS-5).

reason: Accepting a webhook reports nothing about whether the agent it started succeeded or what it produced. Narrowed: the delivery record names the session ids, so an operator can open the session.
justification: Deliberate: DH-ADR-XHOOKS-5 says 'no completion report ... the record names the session to look at'; the session a rule starts is an ordinary session that the webhook runtime no longer owns once the prompt is admitted; a completion report would need the runtime to watch sessions, which the wire decision DH-ADR-WIRE-12 avoids.

reason: The two free web translation endpoints (Google, Bing) may refuse requests or disappear, and a failed request does not fall back to another provider. Only an installation whose operator added the web provider meets this limit.
justification: The endpoints belong to other vendors and no design choice here can make them reliable. The owner decided how far they reach (DH-ADR-36): the web provider is specified but not in the shipped bundle, which translates with the user's own model; an operator may add it in a layer, where it is off by default and counts as a sender (DH-ADR-XMISC-5). A failure is one logged outcome with Retry.

reason: A translation of the model's reasoning may change the inline formatting of the prose; the original is one click away. (Removed: code blocks, math and tables are never sent to a translator, so code cannot be changed.)
justification: Machine translation of prose can move or drop inline markup whatever the provider; that is the behaviour of the translating service or model, not of the harness. DH-D-XMISC-1 excludes code from what is sent.

reason: Register entry U-K2-13, resolved in the convergence round. A session nobody drives, such as a finished subagent session, can get a new translation: the two translation event types are declared log-only, and the service writes them with the session area's AppendLogOnly (DH-D-SESSION-9), which takes a free session's lease for the one append without creating an agent or running a hook (DH-ADR-XMISC-4). Tests DH-T-XMISC-2 and DH-T-SESSION-20. A narrower case is left and is new, not upstream's: when another dsh process holds the session, the translation is refused with translate/session-held-elsewhere and the view says which process to use. core-session.md says in one place that a translation succeeds in that case too; the two documents disagree and x-recommendations-misc.md is the more specific.
Whether the two web translation endpoints can be reached from mainland China depends on the user's network. Only an installation whose operator added the web provider meets this limit.
justification: Reachability of a third party's endpoint from a given network is outside any design. The one egress proxy policy applies to these requests, an unreachable endpoint is one classified failure, and the shipped bundle translates with the user's own model through a route the user already reaches (DH-ADR-36).

reason: The collapsed summary of a reasoning block stays in the original language; translation starts only when the reader expands the block, and it may change the formatting of prose.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words since the final re-check: DH-ADR-XMISC-4 has 'Scope boundary of this record: translation starts only when the reader expands a reasoning block, and the collapsed summary stays in the original language, because every translation is a logged provider call that costs tokens and sends text out'. The formatting half is the machine-translation fact carried under unit client-ui-cot-translation.2.

reason: The free web translation endpoints may fail, limit requests or change their response format. (Removed: saved translations are declared event types, no longer best-effort records.)
justification: The endpoints are another vendor's and stay outside the project's control. A changed response format is caught by the strict decoder as one classified error. By owner decision DH-ADR-36 the web provider is not in the shipped bundle; where an operator adds it, DH-ADR-XMISC-5 keeps it off until chosen.

reason: The harness never looks through a conversation in the background to find something to recommend and keeps no profile of the user; a suggestion is made only inside a turn the user started, when the model uses the skill there. (Removed: a suggestion no longer needs the exact live root agent.)
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words since the final re-check: DH-ADR-XMISC-3 has 'Scope boundary of this record: a suggestion is made only inside a turn the user started, when the model uses the skill there; no background call looks through a conversation for something to recommend and no profile of the user is stored', because either would send data without a user action (DH-ADR-9). The record does not promise 'only when asked': inside a user's turn the model may suggest a feature unprompted, which the reason now says.

reason: The all-prompts title provider treats every eligible user message equally, with no setting to weight or filter them; when the text is too long, the reduction favours the first and the newest prompts.
justification: Deliberate, and stated in the record's own words since the fix pass: DH-ADR-XMISC-6 has 'Scope boundary of this record: every eligible user prompt counts equally, with no setting to weight or filter prompts; when the prompts exceed the byte limit the reduction keeps the first and the newest ones'.

reason: Keeping an adequate title is an instruction to the model, so the model may still reword it. The one deterministic part is built: a returned title equal to the current one after normalisation writes no new title event.
justification: Whether two different titles mean the same is a judgement only a model can make, and a model's output is not deterministic; no semantic check exists to build. A user who wants a fixed title pins it, which stops automatic titles.

reason: The two browser translation endpoints are unofficial: their owners guarantee no availability, quota, response format or regional reachability.
justification: No design can give a guarantee the endpoint's owner does not give. The owner decided to keep the web provider specified but out of the shipped bundle (DH-ADR-36): the shipped bundle translates with the user's own model, which is the path with a supported interface; an operator may add the web provider in a layer, where no provider is preselected and the sender is off until turned on (DH-ADR-XMISC-5).

reason: The cause is an update made of two separate profile operations. The Go manager has no update operation: every management operation is one write of the profile layer under one lock, followed by reconciliation, so no other operation can run inside it. The one copy an add needs (the extension area's approved copy, DH-ADR-EXT-3) is made before that write and is merely unreferenced if the write fails. A replaced plugin takes effect when it is added again, because a grant binds to the approved bytes and a different digest is a different plugin.

The cause is that the host itself loads a package's JavaScript, so a replaced package needs a new process. A plugin's code runs in its own process, from an approved copy in the harness home (DH-ADR-EXT-3). A changed directory takes effect when the owner adds it again, which approves the new bytes and runs them as that one entry, in any profile; the host is never restarted for it.

The cause is that a start-up-only profile cannot unload modules it loaded, so their package cannot be removed while it runs. In Go a management change always reconciles the running tree whether or not file watching is on. Removal unloads the entry's fiber and deletes the entry; the operator's directory is never changed, and the approved copy and the plugin's state go only with an explicit purge (test DH-T-BOOT-20). A running plugin can therefore be removed in every profile.

The cause is that an operation spans a package-manager run that writes many files and cannot be undone. A Go management operation downloads nothing and writes one file atomically. An add first lets the extension area make one approved copy of the plugin's bytes in the harness home (DH-ADR-EXT-3); if the write of the entry then fails, the copy is unreferenced, nothing runs, and retention removes it. The only split outcome is saved but not applied, which the result reports as two separate facts.

Upstream's tool asked for its own approval inside its body. The Go tool asks nothing and changes nothing durable: by owner decision DH-ADR-30 it has list, inspect, attach and detach only, and it never writes the profile. The one consent an attachment needs is an interaction that the extension area asks through the interaction registry (DH-ADR-EXT-8), so no action can forget a gate. Test DH-T-BOOT-21 checks through the real pipeline that the profile layer is byte-identical after every action.

A custom profile in Go extends a built-in profile and has only its own layer, so it cannot omit the bundle that mounts the ACP server (boot.md, DH-ADR-BOOT-1). The carrier entry wire.acp is on the required-entry list, so a carrier that fails to load stops start-up with a report instead of leaving a client waiting.

A custom profile in Go extends a built-in profile and cannot omit the bundle that mounts the SDK server, and the carrier entry wire.sdk is a required entry, so a carrier that fails to load stops start-up with a report instead of leaving the client's initialization without a peer.

Upstream's hold misses a message that arrives during a turn or other maintenance. The Go design has no hold: creation from the UI is its own operation offered only before the first turn, a message sent meanwhile is latched by the driver, and a failed attempt blocks step 1 through a PreStep listener (DH-ADR-XFORGE-8). Recovery of a worktree removed by hand is settled with the session-views area (x-forge-worktree.md section 10, item 2): DH-ADR-VIEW-8 keeps every tool-made move inside the anchor, and recovery of a missing directory goes through workdir.Access with the reason recover, which this area denies for a recorded worktree so that the card offers Restore instead of falling back silently.

The limit concerns how an npm registry update saves version specs and where a reinstalled bundle lands in the bundle order; there are no registry updates, and a profile's bundle order is fixed in the binary (DH-ADR-BOOT-1).

Dropped by DH-ADR-13 (no plugin download). The limit concerns console prompts and timeouts of the Git transport probe that precedes a pnpm install of a fetched plugin; the Go manager fetches nothing and starts no Git process.
Dropped by DH-ADR-13 (no auto-update). The limit concerns pnpm build-script approval during an npm version update; there are no plugin updates, and no build scripts run.
Dropped by DH-ADR-18 (no desktop application). The limit concerns package operations owned by the Electron desktop shell.
Dropped by DH-ADR-17 (the in-browser preview runtime is not built). The limit concerns the WebWorker packer's static discovery of JavaScript dependencies for that runtime.

Dropped by DH-ADR-18 (no desktop application) and DH-ADR-UTIL-3, which records that listing the applications that can open a file is not built (also DH-ADR-UISIDE-8). The limit describes icon extraction for the application picker of upstream's desktop integration.

Dropped by DH-ADR-13 (plugins come from local directories; nothing is discovered or downloaded). The public-npm-only limit concerns reading a package's files from npm file CDNs for a plugin detail page.
Dropped by DH-ADR-13 and DH-ADR-BOOT-11 (no plugin market). The limit concerns a generator's obligations toward an index of npm packages, which the Go design never reads.
Dropped by DH-ADR-13 and DH-ADR-BOOT-11 (no plugin market). The missing size bound concerns parsing a fetched market index document, which the Go design never fetches or parses.

Dropped by DH-ADR-13 (no plugin market; the generator is not built, DH-ADR-WEBAPP-8). The limit concerns how the generator fetches Git commits.
Dropped by DH-ADR-13 (no plugin market; the generator is not built, DH-ADR-WEBAPP-8). The limit concerns the generator's npm registry access; the Go design reads no npm registry.
Dropped by DH-ADR-13 (no plugin market; the generator is not built, DH-ADR-WEBAPP-8). The limit concerns the generator's Git credential handling.

Dropped by DH-ADR-XFORGE-5 (the changes view is not built) and DH-ADR-38 (status only). The limit describes placeholder heights of file sections that the React view had not drawn yet.
